exposure: Maternal vaginal colonization with Group B Streptococcus (GBS)
Maternal vaginal colonization with Staphylococcus aureus
Maternal vaginal colonization with E. coli
Maternal vaginal colonization with Lactobacillus species
cohort: The study included 150 newborns and their mothers from a tertiary care hospital in Bihar, India, focusing on those affected by early neonatal septicemia.
finding: Maternal colonization with Group B Streptococcus (GBS) and anaerobes was significantly associated with early-onset neonatal septicemia, while the presence of Lactobacillus species was associated with a lower frequency of the condition.
